title: Understanding Mean Cubed Error
text: The Mean Cubed Error is calculated by taking the average of the cube of the differences between the actual and predicted values. Think about how cubing a number affects its magnitude, especially when the number is negative.

title: Impact of Cubing on Errors
text: When you cube a negative number, the result is negative, but its magnitude increases. Consider how this might affect the penalty for underpredictions compared to overpredictions.

hintAnswer: Cubing a negative error results in a larger negative value than cubing a positive error of the same magnitude.
title: Comparing Underpredictions and Overpredictions
text: Which of the following statements is true about the effect of cubing on negative and positive errors?
choices: Cubing a negative error results in a larger negative value than cubing a positive error of the same magnitude.
Cubing a positive error results in a larger positive value than cubing a negative error of the same magnitude.
Cubing affects positive and negative errors equally.
